instruments.evidence: App.tsx (a pathless lazy layout route around the nine /omnichat routes), OmniChatCallLayout.tsx (new), OmniChatHeader.tsx, OmniChatCreditsMenu.tsx, LiveCallControls.tsx, OmniChatChatPage.tsx, and tests. Boundaries: router -> layout -> call provider context -> header and chat page; chat page -> startVoiceCall; header -> credits menu and live controls.

Read f6fa4f256 (credits label read aloud, credits zero while loading, video usage field) and c7191c885 (hang-up button name changed every second). The hang-up label is still static and the timer a separate role=timer span in the printed markup ("End the call with Sadie", "Call time 12:34"); the credits button still names loading as loading.

instruments.why: No prompt, request or message is assembled differently: startCall(conversationId, 'voice') is the B1 provider's, unchanged; the chat page passes (conversation 42, {id, name}), asserted by the chat page test.

instruments.evidence: Printed the real LiveCallControls (mute, "End the call with Sadie", 12:34, role=timer "Call time 12:34"), the real credits button ("1,250 OmniCredits"), and the real header for three states: in a call, a failed call, no call.

The voice paywall key 'voice_call' is a member of OmniChatPaywallFeature and renders 'Unlock voice calls' (asserted). The nine route paths inside the layout route are the same strings as before (read back from App.tsx).
The chat page passes { id: activePersona.id, name: activePersona.name }, the OmniChatCallPersona shape; the header reads calls.call and calls.failure, the fields the provider sets.

One call at a time lives in two places: the provider hangs up before a new voice call, and the chat page hangs up a voice call before a video call opens (asserted: endCall once, then the video dialog).

instruments.why: No worker or external contract changed.
No field added to a struct that crosses a boundary.

instruments.evidence: The reader is useOmniChatCall through the real layout route: a probe with the real OmniChatCallLayout under MemoryRouter showed the provider present on two OmniChat pages with the same call, and absent outside, where endCall ran once with the session id.

The header markup the browser measured was rendered by the real components in jsdom, signed in, with the real credits menu and live controls. The first measurement used the signed-out account button (52 px) and was wrong; every later one used the signed-in button (78 px) and the worst content: a 12,500 balance and a 1:02:34 timer.

Every place that starts an OmniChat call: grep finds only the chat page (two phone buttons, two video buttons); the header is the only other surface and carries the controls on every page through OmniChatShell.

OmniChatCallModal's voice branch (the voice start, liveCallId, useLiveVoiceCall for voice) is now unreachable: the page opens it only with mode="video". Deliberate and told to the user: it is removed with the call-screen lint phase, which edits the same file, to keep B2 within five files.

startVoiceCall rejects only with OmniChatCallPaymentRequired, which opens the voice paywall (asserted); anything else is rethrown rather than swallowed. The provider reports the other start failures itself (the failure banner).
Guests are stopped before the provider: requestCall opens the sign-in modal first. The header shows the controls whatever the auth state, since only a signed-in user can have a call.
The compact prop added in the first fix was removed again: the chevron rule is now one class in each component, not a flag passed down.

Having found the phone overflow, the same shape was measured at every width and state: 640-750 px during a call (found b2-exit-overlaps-at-tablet) and the no-call signed-in header at 360-375 px (found the logo squeeze in b2-header-chevrons-crowd-phone).

instruments.why: No goroutine or Go shared state.

instruments.evidence: Leaving OmniChat unmounts the layout and ends the call: the navigation probe showed endCall called once with the session after leaving, none while moving between OmniChat pages.
Four controls, each reverting one fix: each named test fails with a real AssertionError with its patch applied and passes at HEAD.
eslint and tsc -b exit 0; vitest on the header, credits menu, live controls, provider and chat page tests: 80 passed.
B6 found all four and no instrument named measuring layout in a real browser; B6 was added to instruments.json.

Nothing starts before the decision: the voice press calls startVoiceCall directly, and the video press ends a voice call before it opens the video screen.

findings.summary: B2 put mute and the live icon into the OmniChat header row as-is; at 360-390 px the row needed 444 px, so mute sat on the logo, the account button was cut in half and the exit fell off the screen.

control.observed: With the patch (the logo no longer hidden on a phone during a call): AssertionError, expected false to be true. Without: passes.

findings.summary: A failed call's reason sat inline in the header row and, measured, wrapped into a 98 px column 172 px tall inside a 72 px header.

tests: src/components/omnichat/__tests__/OmniChatHeader.test.tsx -t 'hangs a failed call below the header'
control.observed: With the patch (the reason back inline): AssertionError, expected false to be true. Without: passes.

findings.summary: Signed in with a five-digit balance, the header at 360-375 px had no room for its two chevrons: during a call the live pill overlapped the credits button, and with no call the logo box shrank to 44 px under the credits button. The first fix was measured with the signed-out account button (52 px, not 78) and missed this.

tests: src/components/omnichat/__tests__/OmniChatHeader.test.tsx -t 'shows the whole header when there is no call'
control.observed: With the patch (both chevrons shown on a phone, the logo shrinkable): both tests fail with AssertionError, expected false to be true. Without: both pass.

findings.summary: From 640 to about 750 px during a call, the logo, the username and the exit's full label all return, and the logo was pushed onto the hang-up button.

tests: src/components/omnichat/__tests__/OmniChatHeader.test.tsx -t 'gives the logo and the exit to a call in progress'
control.observed: With the patch (the exit back from 640 px during a call): AssertionError, expected false to be true. Without: passes.
